exceptions.detail: Single, multiple and range selection follow React DayPicker's endpoint, minimum and maximum rules. Calendar uses variable week counts, shared square day highlights, today/range active fills, caption dropdowns, disabled dates, inclusive whole-day bounds, week numbers, responsive month layouts and arrow/Home/End/Page navigation. Date Picker supports an empty value, shared field/popup surfaces, date bounds and dismissal on selection. Month/year granularities use twelve-cell, three-column grids, whole-period bounds, first-day values, twelve-year page boundaries, arrow/Page navigation, current/selected states and shared directional page motion. Day glyphs retain density size; native hit slots prefer 44 points and shrink to the glyph size when constrained, with horizontal overflow for larger text. Editable Date Picker fields commit canonical relative/localized/custom-format text on Return or blur, preserve invalid text, clear optional values and retain required values. The calendar action and Option+Down open the parsed period and restore text focus on dismissal. Text parsing uses Gregorian/ISO calendars and installed date-fns locales; relative phrases are English. Day-and-time selection uses the shared wheel, preserves the clock across day changes, stays open while selecting and commits same-day clock changes. Editable date-time text splits the canonical date and time forms, retaining invalid time drafts. Composite range fields remain incomplete. Calendar custom day renderers, modifiers, presets, alternate calendar systems, right-to-left navigation and complete keyboard/VoiceOver, fresh React, minimum-OS and physical-device qualification remain open.

Standalone Time Wheel uses the canonical active band, tabular 16-point labels, edge fade and drum tilt, with 12/24-hour clocks, seconds, minute steps, clock bounds, center snapping, keyboard navigation and native adjustable actions. Date bindings preserve their calendar day and normalize skipped DST clock times forward. Dynamic Type grows row height and measured column widths; scoped motion-off and Reduce Motion remove tilt and automatic movement. Time Input uses an editable shared field, canonical compact/AM-PM/named-time parsing, optional clearing and required-value retention. Its iOS nonmodal popup keeps typing available, respects the keyboard viewport and restores field focus. Height composition and Date Picker integration are implemented. macOS text-focus behavior, full VoiceOver, fresh React frame comparison, minimum-runtime and physical-device qualification remain open.

Day, days, week, month and agenda layouts, create/edit/duplicate/delete, undo/redo, overlap columns, native drag/resize, 17 canonical event colors and scoped recurring edit/delete are implemented. The locally bundled canonical recurrence engine passes actual JavaScriptCore Intl/DST fixtures. Calendar-source filter UI, business-hour constraints, week-number options and custom hue/chroma configuration remain incomplete; full gesture and keyboard parity is not certified.

TextKit 2 and NSTextView use the canonical block schema and local JavaScriptCore engine for projection, transactions, nested lists, Markdown round-trip, formatting, links, GFM table/code editors, selection and undo/redo. The primary fixture is React's notes document. Document sizes are density independent, UIKit retains exact Inter axes/italic and Geist Mono through live text-size updates, and code uses its own density role with token emphasis/comment slant and noninteractive link underlines. Initial state stays unselected until focus; the automatic minimum follows six document lines and Dynamic Type. Toolbar groups, active fills, focus ring, footer word counting and a native caret/selection keyboard accessory are implemented. Both adapters flush pending canonical content/selection before focus and distinguish replacement state objects sharing revisions. UIKit task controls expose checked/disabled state, press/check motion and hit areas bounded before editable text; task activation selects its caret and participates in undo. Read-only task/block edits are ignored while copying remains available. UIKit Copy controls expose accessibility labels and two-second success-colored checks without focusing or selecting the document. In-document images still use the attachment box; native code wraps and block editors use sheets. Full slash/bubble/link-surface parity, exact inline/underline geometry, rich table-cell marks, block dragging and arbitrary kit extension UI remain incomplete; AppKit task/code decorations differ. Fresh React, full keyboard/VoiceOver, minimum-OS and physical-device qualification remain open.

All 32 published block variants have distinct native compositions, fields, Fabricator icons and action callbacks. Four auth-validation fixtures and catalog route smoke tests pass. Every variant's responsive visual details, keyboard traversal and assistive-technology behavior have not been individually compared against web. App-shell-04 window dragging depends on host-window integration.

All 14 shapes, three eye styles, 10 states, 17 named colors, custom color contrast and pointer gaze use canonical geometry and tokens. Native display-cadence contour interpolation, state morphs and anchored-body eye projection exist. Sample loops do not cover every independent canonical gesture period; exact contour correspondence during rapid cross-state changes still needs qualification.

Distinct chart geometries, typed series, series visibility, legends, selection inspectors, keyboard actions and accessible data tables are implemented where applicable. StatusBar models real uptime periods. Sankey uses the canonical weighted graph layout with numeric fixtures. Complete web option surfaces and reveal/morph animations remain incomplete; every layout/interaction combination is not qualified. Canvas Sankey transitions currently apply immediately.

The canonical default light/dark palette, three densities, Inter variable weights, numbered surface shadows, shared motion and icon geometry are generated. Core Text uses the web's exact 450/550 weights with optical sizing; Dynamic Type and motion settings propagate to iOS overlays. Complete runtime look presets, role hue/chroma, surface tint and font customization options are not exposed by the native theme API.

Inter's actual variation axes and optical sizing pass native tests. Default compact/default/spacious control geometry remains 28/36/44 points, and enlarged controls and scoped popup text pass accessibility-size regressions. Card, field and dialog text use the CSS line-height treatment. Full per-component line wrapping, every Dynamic Type category, Bold Text and current neutral web screenshot comparisons remain unqualified.

Image/fallback rendering uses an opaque background, the shared medium weight, fixed-size initials and a full-name image accessibility element. Group hover parting, grouped tooltips and all web part/variant options are not implemented.

Read-only string cells use shared header/body/footer typography, density padding, 60% dividers, measured column widths and horizontal overflow. Footer rows, preferred widths and emphasized columns support the React invoice fixture. A large-text overflow regression passes. Arbitrary cell views, grouped headers and column spans are not exposed; full keyboard/VoiceOver, pointer-glide verification and fresh web comparison remain unqualified.

The icon media tile uses surface-4 geometry/shadows, 14-point semibold titles, relaxed 13-point descriptions and shared spacing. Action content is a native view builder, with the React project actions in the explorer. Default/custom media and every web composition option are not exposed; fresh web and complete accessibility qualification remain open.

Checkboxes draw the canonical short-leg-first mark with enter/exit timing; radio groups move one persistent full-size dot; switches use canonical thumb travel and hover/press geometry. All three show invalid, disabled and focused states with medium-weight labels. iOS row gaps keep adjacent 44-point hit targets separate. Selected/mixed values, disabled states and exclusive radio selection pass UI regressions. Complete keyboard traversal, VoiceOver speech, rapid interruption and fresh web frame-by-frame comparison remain unqualified.

Single selection, explicit empty folders, inherited disabled states, muted labels, canonical light/dark file artwork, scrolling, guides, moving selection/hover surfaces, arrow/Home/End navigation, sibling expansion, typeahead and file-open callbacks are implemented. iOS rows preserve 44-point touch targets while macOS uses density height. Multiple/range selection, delete/undo, context callbacks and drag/drop are not exposed. Complete keyboard/VoiceOver, pointer interruption, minimum-OS and fresh React screenshot/motion qualification remain open. Optional File Tree PNGs total 522304 bytes before packaging; foundations exclude them.

All 12 value types, type-aware filters/sorting, editing, selection, column order/resize/hide/pin, metadata changes, grouping, typed calculations and local paging are implemented. Cells preserve primary identifiers, option labels/images, status dots, all tags, link destinations, Boolean editing, numeric precision and relative-date thresholds. JavaScript fractional ISO timestamps parse, date calculations stay absolute and edited status option ordering affects sort. Widths, resize minimums, alignment and first sort direction come from the canonical generated type defaults; header sorts reverse and clear on repeated taps. Sort headers resolve their own descriptor and use shared type/arrow motion without platform press dimming. The demo uses React's seeded accounts; queries run above local hover/focus/viewport state and pagination builds only visible controls. Complete settings/view variants, numbered rows, header-anchored filter/editor surfaces, labeled option choices in editors/filters, floating selection actions, pin-edge fades, remote data-provider/windowing APIs, full spreadsheet range paste and all web keyboard shortcuts remain incomplete. Fresh React screenshot/motion, full VoiceOver, minimum-OS, macOS window and physical-device performance qualification remain open.

Markdown and Syntax Highlight use the canonical parser/tree/tokenizer through the local JavaScriptCore adapter. Native document sizes, marked text, nested/ordered lists, readonly tasks, GFM tables, quotes, code-fence metadata, image views and raw unsupported source are implemented. Code uses Geist Mono, shared token colors, file headers, line numbers/markers, wrap, capped scrolling and edge fades; native clipboard feedback resets after two seconds. Main demo data comes from React's fixtures, and a full-source clipboard round-trip passes. Exact inline-code chip padding/corners, custom renderer/kit/grammar APIs, optional code-header composition and complete selection/VoiceOver/media failure-state qualification remain incomplete; fresh React and minimum-OS comparisons remain open.
Color/document pickers, context menus and AVKit retain Apple input and dismissal semantics. Their system chrome is platform-specific; web pixel parity is not claimed.

Fabricator popup/dialog/sheet surfaces and enter/exit timings, scoped motion settings, Select content sizing/search reset, sliding tab selection and switch thumb motion are implemented. Select sizing/search and repeated dialog dismissal passed iPhone and iPad regressions. Complete keyboard focus restoration, long-list and large-text coverage, nested overlays, gesture interruption and frame-by-frame comparison with current React captures remain unqualified.

The web header's actions and its page menu (AppShellHeaderActions with menu, added 2026-11-17: page settings behind one ellipsis on every width, joined by the folded actions on phones) have no SwiftUI equivalent yet.

verification.consumerInstallation: Published items and all distinct source closures are checked as clean standalone macOS consumers; current counts and results are linked from the comparison ledger
verification.iOS: simulator app builds; earlier smoke tests passed all 141 catalog routes. Regressions cover canonical Markdown content, a full-source native clipboard round-trip with feedback reset, wrapped/capped code, File Tree navigation/open/state behavior, table overflow, field feedback, dialogs, Dynamic Type popups, avatar semantics and selection controls. Relay Return/Home/End and visible tree focus were inspected separately from XCTest's named-key synthesis; current summaries are linked from the comparison ledger
verification.iPadOS: document, typography, selection, forms, dialogs and File Tree regressions pass; light/dark and large-text captures inspected through Relay. Latest result summaries are linked from the comparison ledger
verification.macOS: arm64 app and Swift package build are checked with canonical document/code, font, model, motion, editor, recurrence, auth and chart tests; current counts and results are linked from the comparison ledger
